rules.sentence: The clear demarcation of ischemic and non-ischemic tracts is typical of occlusive ischemic conditions, even if in NOMI the colonic involvement may vary based on the susceptibility of the bowel wall to ischemia.

Typhlitis is typically localized in the cecal area, while in acute appendicitis we may see a variable inflammatory involvement of the adjacent bowel, in radiation colitis there is a segmental involvement of the irradiated bowel, and in infectious colitis the extent of involvement may vary and can manifest as pancolitis.
